what: Minecraft's time as a world.clock@1 ClockPort: the game's own world clocks, timelines and time packet from 26.1 (native-clock); before it, the overworld clock is vanilla's dayTime and a mod's own clocks live in saved data on the overworld, advanced on the server tick and synced by a payload the mod delivers (emulated-clock). Everything arithmetic is the pure model's.

overlays.why: the clock manager exposes a clock's state only as a packed copy, reports a move as a flag, and a client can read only total ticks (26.3 gives each clock an instance and a move three outcomes)
saved data is a loader function and a supplier, saved by save(CompoundTag); there is no tick rate manager
saved data is a Factory, saved by save(CompoundTag); there is still no tick rate manager
the tick rate manager arrives; saved data is still a Factory saved by save(CompoundTag)
saved data is a SavedDataType with a codec
game rules become registry-backed (GameRules.ADVANCE_TIME) and are read from a level
